# Streamweld 1.0.1

- Stop a saved AI SDK chat after a page reload without reconnecting or replaying
  its response. Failed stop requests keep the checkpoint for retry; a newer
  generation started by the same transport is preserved during the request.
- Use `--version` on the proxy, operator, or CLI to print the release version,
  commit, and commit date. Proxy `--help` works with invalid environment settings
  and displays built-in defaults.
- Verify the built client with native Deno 2.9.6 and Bun 1.4.2 HTTP tests before
  publishing, alongside Node 20, 22, and 24. A browser import check rejects
  Node-only dependencies; it does not test streaming in a browser or edge host.

## Upgrade

No protocol, checkpoint format, or public TypeScript signature changes.
Update both npm packages together when using the AI SDK adapter:

```sh
npm install @streamweld/client@1.0.1
npm install @streamweld/ai-sdk@1.0.1 ai@^5
```

For Kubernetes:

```sh
helm upgrade --install streamweld oci://ghcr.io/satwiksps/charts/streamweld \
  --namespace streamweld-system --create-namespace \
  --version 1.0.1 --wait --timeout 3m
```

Binaries are attached with SHA-256 checksums. Container images are
`ghcr.io/satwiksps/streamweld-proxy:1.0.1` and
`ghcr.io/satwiksps/streamweld-operator:1.0.1`.

The [AI SDK setup notes](https://github.com/satwiksps/streamweld/blob/v1.0.1/packages/ai-sdk/README.md)
cover React, strict TypeScript checks, and the tested dependency override.
One low-severity upstream AI SDK advisory remains after that override.

Memory-mode proxies and embedded Redis use `Recreate` updates. Memory journals
and Redis without persistence lose retained streams on replacement. Run
`streamweldctl doctor` against your exact backend/model/tokenizer before
enabling migration; GPU model compatibility is not established by these tests.
